description: Linchpin hybrid maintenance window: routing only. Non-majors and lock-file maintenance stack on the current maintenance/YYYY-MM window, which merges with one review; majors are raised against the default branch as their own PRs. Linchpin's own packages skip the window and go straight to the default branch. Add it AFTER github>linchpin/renovatebot-config or github>linchpin/renovatebot-config:automerge; it does not extend either, so it cannot re-apply the default preset's rules over the automerge ones. Consume as github>linchpin/renovatebot-config:maintenance-window.

packageRules.description: Majors never ride in the window. Each is its own reviewed PR against the default branch, so one breaking major cannot strand the batch - maintenance/2026-07 on linchpin.com carried three majors and a Babel 8 regression, and its safe bumps had to be salvaged by hand.

Non-majors and lock-file maintenance stack on the window, where one review merges the month, and never on the default branch. Negated rather than naming main, because some repositories default to master.

Linchpin's own packages skip the window. Each release was already reviewed and released from its own repository, so waiting a month to consume it only delays it: an update to discovery or linchpin-blocks goes straight to the default branch, where the consuming repository's own automerge rules apply. The list is explicit because linchpin/** also covers third-party plugins mirrored on packagist.linchpin.com (Gravity Forms, WooCommerce Subscriptions, WooCommerce API Manager, Pressable Cache Management, spellbook); those are someone else's releases and stay in the window. Add a Linchpin package here the first time a repository consumes it. This rule must stay AFTER the non-major rule above, because the later rule wins.
The other half of the rule above: Linchpin's own packages never ride in a window, so one release cannot arrive twice, once on the default branch and again in the month's batch.
